title: Packers Snag Former Cowboys OG Tomlinson from Practice Squad, Boosting Offensive Line Depth
body:
Green Bay’s offensive line received a timely boost on Tuesday as the Packers announced the acquisition of veteran guard Laken Tomlinson, who was lifted from the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. The move, confirmed by NFL insiders, gives the struggling unit a seasoned presence ahead of a crucial stretch of games and signals the organization’s willingness to address depth concerns before the trade deadline.

Tomlinson, 30, brings a decade of NFL experience, having spent the bulk of his career with the San Francisco 49ers before joining Dallas in 2023. Over 121 games, he has started 82 at both guard and tackle, earning a reputation for reliable run blocking and solid pass‑set technique. While his tenure with the Cowboys this season was limited to practice‑squad duties, his familiarity with pro‑level schemes and veteran leadership are assets the Packers hope to translate into immediate on‑field improvement.

The Packers’ offensive line has been a focal point of criticism this season, with injuries and inconsistent play contributing to a league‑worst ranking in sacks allowed through the first ten weeks. Starting right guard Elgton Jenkins suffered a season‑ending knee injury in Week 8, and the team has rotated several backups to fill the void, none of whom have provided the stability needed to protect quarterback Jordan Love. By adding Tomlinson, Green Bay not only gains a capable interior lineman but also a mentor who can help accelerate the development of younger players like rookie right tackle Jordan Brown and second‑year guard Zachary Carter.

From a strategic standpoint, the signing aligns with head coach Matt LaFleur’s broader emphasis on protecting the quarterback and establishing a more balanced ground attack. Last season, Green Bay’s rushing yards per attempt ranked in the bottom third of the league, a shortfall that often forced the offense into predictable passing situations. Tomlinson’s proven run‑blocking pedigree—he helped pave the way for the 49ers’ dominant rushing attacks in 2019 and 2020—could be instrumental in opening lanes for running back Aaron Jones, who has been limited by inconsistent blocking. Moreover, the veteran’s versatility allows him to slide between guard spots, giving LaFleur additional flexibility in game‑planning and in‑game adjustments.

The transaction also reflects the Packers’ proactive approach to roster management as the trade deadline approaches. While many teams have been busy shuffling draft picks and high‑profile players, Green Bay has opted for low‑cost, high‑value depth moves. Tomlinson’s contract is modest—a week‑to‑week practice‑squad salary converted to a standard rookie‑minimum deal—meaning the financial impact is negligible against the backdrop of the team’s salary‑cap situation. This prudent use of resources underscores a front office strategy that prioritizes positional depth without mortgaging future flexibility.

Looking ahead, the true measure of Tomlinson’s impact will be seen in the upcoming weeks against formidable opponents such as the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions, both of whom feature aggressive defensive fronts. If the veteran can quickly integrate into LaFleur’s scheme and shore up the interior line, Green Bay could see a reduction in pressure rates and a more sustained rushing rhythm—both critical components for a playoff push. As the season enters its decisive phase, the Packers’ ability to blend seasoned veterans like Tomlinson with emerging talent may prove decisive in turning a middling offensive line into a competitive unit capable of supporting a deep postseason run.
